title: perf: streamline model catalog rendering
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Renders only the active desktop or mobile model row layout and switches automatically at the existing responsive breakpoint without a first-paint layout flip.
- Progressively mounts 24 model rows at a time while scrolling, reducing the initial Official catalog from about 17,400 DOM elements to about 2,500.
- Preserves row state while filtering instead of remounting the complete model list on every search keystroke.
- Reuses dashboard session and loader data for 30 seconds while allowing failed session checks to retry immediately.
- Reorders Official tabs to match the API: All, Text, Image, Video, 3D, Audio, Realtime, Embedding.

Browser find-in-page only searches rows currently mounted; the catalog search continues to search every model.

Checks: `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build:frontend`; Biome; 38 focused pricing/model tests. The full suite reached 675 passing tests; 62 Stripe integration tests require the unavailable local `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and are unrelated to this frontend change.

gist.headline: The catalog stopped hauling furniture
gist.blurb: The model catalog now brings in rows a little at a time instead of unpacking the whole warehouse at once. Polli kept the labels in API order, because even bees appreciate a tidy shelf.
gist.summary: The dashboard model catalog now renders only the active responsive row layout, progressively mounts 24 rows while scrolling, cuts the initial Official catalog from roughly 17,400 to 2,500 DOM elements, preserves rows during search filtering, and caches session/loader data for 30 seconds.
gist.impact: Browsing, filtering, and opening the Official model catalog should feel substantially lighter, while the tabs now follow the API order: All, Text, Image, Video, 3D, Audio, Realtime, Embedding.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy model-library garden: Polli, wearing a tiny librarian visor, sorts compact model cards into neat shelves while a CRT monitor robot cheerfully wheels in just one small stack at a time. A scrolling vine represents progressive loading, with the full catalog still searchable through a glowing terminal; tidy category tabs sit above the shelves.
